name: p2-2019-budget-minutes
title: Error budget: 0.1 percent of 43,200 minutes
spec: Top: a formula strip in monospace 'Error budget = 100 percent minus the SLO'. Below, a 30-day window bar drawn as a long horizontal bar labelled '30 x 24 x 60 = 43,200 minutes'. A thin orange slice at the right end labelled '0.1 percent = 43.2 minutes of full outage'. Under the bar a small table with four rows, columns 'SLO', 'Budget fraction', 'Minutes per 30 days': '99 percent, 0.01, 432'; '99.9 percent, 0.001, 43.2' (orange outline); '99.95 percent, 0.0005, 21.6'; '99.99 percent, 0.0001, 4.32'. A side card for requests: 'At 100 requests per second, 30 days = 259,200,000 requests; 0.1 percent allows 259,200 failed requests'. Caption: 'The budget turns a vague target into a number you can spend.'
alt: An error budget is 100 percent minus the SLO, so a 99.9 percent target over 30 days allows 43.2 minutes of full outage.
cap: The error budget is 100 percent minus the SLO, so 99.9 percent over 30 days allows 43.2 minutes of full outage.

name: p2-2019-symptom-cause
title: Pages are for symptoms; causes become tickets
spec: Left column: a cause card 'GPU utilisation 98 percent' with a dashed outline and the note 'High utilisation is the goal, not a fault'. An arrow to a box 'Alert at 3 a.m.' with a red bell. A second example card: 'Replica restarts: a cause' with the note 'Restart count goes up'. Right column: a symptom card 'Users see errors or slow responses' drawn with an orange outline. A two-lane split at the bottom: left lane 'Page: burn-rate alerts on gateway availability and gateway TTFT' with a green pager icon; right lane 'Ticket: causes such as KV cache above 95 percent for 15 minutes, repeated preemptions' with a grey ticket icon. A caption: 'Ask whether a user sees it. If yes, it is a symptom and can page.'
anchor: ### 7. Symptoms, not causes, and what pages
alt: A high GPU utilisation alert is a cause and not a fault, so pages come from user-visible symptoms such as burn-rate alerts while causes become tickets.
cap: Pages come from user-visible symptoms such as burn-rate alerts on gateway availability and TTFT, while causes such as high KV cache usage become tickets.

name: p2-2019-goodput-split
title: Throughput counts everything; goodput counts what met the target
spec: A split bar of 40,000 tokens per second drawn as one long bar. The bar is divided into two segments: a green segment labelled 'Tokens that met the TTFT and per-token limits' and a grey segment labelled 'Tokens that arrived too late for anyone to care'. A label above the whole bar 'Throughput: 40,000 tokens per second'. A label above the green segment 'Goodput: only work that met both targets'. A small chart beside it with two lines over time: 'Throughput: climbs when batch size rises' and 'Goodput: falls at the same time' drawn in orange. Formula card in monospace: 'Goodput = requests per second meeting both limits / all requests per second'. Bottom green bar: 'Report goodput next to throughput, because only goodput falls when users suffer.'
alt: Throughput of 40,000 tokens per second includes tokens that arrive too late, while goodput counts only requests that met both the TTFT and per-token limits.
cap: Throughput of 40,000 tokens per second includes tokens that arrived too late, while goodput counts only the requests that met both limits.

name: p2-2019-cashier-kitchen
title: Measure at the gateway, explain at the engine
spec: A two-part layout. Left part: a gateway box labelled 'Gateway: nearest the customer, SLO ratios come from here' with a cashier icon, and an arrow from the customer icon into it. Right part: an engine box labelled 'Engine: queue, prefill and decode, KV cache use, preemptions' with a kitchen icon. An arrow from the gateway into a router queue box labelled 'Request waits in the router queue, six seconds in the example'. A dashed arrow from the gateway back toward the engine labelled 'Explains why an order was slow'. Retry loop drawn between gateway and engine: 'Retry hides the first failure, so count the outcome the customer sees'. A stream card: 'Gateway sends 200 at the first token: count a stream good only if it ends with a normal finish'. Orange outline on the retry loop. Bottom note: 'The engine cannot report that it is dead, because it is the thing that died.'
anchor: ### 11. Measure at the gateway, explain at the engine
alt: The gateway measures the outcome the customer sees and the engine explains why, with retries and streams counted by their final outcome.
cap: The gateway measures what the customer sees, and the engine explains why, counting retries and streams by their final outcome.

name: p2-2019-slo-chain
title: From user outcome to SLI to SLO to error budget
spec: A left-to-right chain of four rounded boxes with arrows between them and a number circle on each. Box 1 'User outcome: did the request succeed fast enough?' with a user icon. Box 2 'SLI: good events divided by all events' with a ratio icon. Box 3 'SLO: the target, for example 99.9 percent' with a target icon. Box 4 'Error budget: 100 percent minus the SLO' with a wallet icon. Arrow from box 4 to a burn-rate gauge labelled 'Burn rate: how fast the budget is spent'. Below box 2 a note 'Count the outcome the customer sees, not each attempt'. Below box 4 a note 'Latency is three numbers, and end-to-end depends on length'. Orange outline on box 3. Caption: 'A token API breaks the usual SLI recipe, so define good events per request outcome.'
anchor: ### 1. A token API breaks the usual SLI recipe
alt: The SLI recipe for a token API runs from user outcome to SLI ratio, SLO target and error budget, with the burn rate showing how fast the budget is spent.
cap: The SLI recipe runs from user outcome to an SLI ratio, an SLO target and an error budget, with the burn rate showing how fast the budget is spent.
